target.title: fix(line): cap message action text length
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

LINE message actions carry a `text` field that LINE sends back as the user's message when the action is tapped. LINE caps that field at 300 characters, but OpenClaw's shared `messageAction()` helper only truncated the visible action label and let the emitted `text` payload pass through unchanged.

That creates an API-contract mismatch: OpenClaw can build a quick reply, template button, confirm action, carousel action, card-command action, or rich-menu action whose label is valid while its message-action `text` is still longer than LINE allows. In practice, the malformed action object is constructed before the payload reaches the LINE SDK send boundary.

The narrow pre-fix trigger was:

```ts
messageAction("Go", "x".repeat(301)).text.length === 301
```

The affected user-realistic path is:

```text
quick replies / template buttons / confirm actions / carousel actions / card commands / rich menus
  -> messageAction(label, text)
  -> LINE SDK payload
  -> LINE Messaging API
```

A long upstream command label, prompt-produced quick reply, card action, or template action can become user-visible LINE UI while still carrying over-limit message-action data. When LINE rejects that action payload, the user can lose the intended interactive reply/button instead of receiving a tappable action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The production change stays at the shared action-constructor boundary, but now uses a LINE message-action-specific grapheme cap instead of the UTF-16 action-data cap used by postback and datetime picker data:

```diff
 export function messageAction(label: string, text?: string): Action {
   return {
     type: "message",
     label: truncateLineActionLabel(label),
-    text: text ?? label,
+    text: truncateLineMessageText(text ?? label),
   };
 }
```

This keeps the fix centralized for all `messageAction()` callers while matching LINE's message-action text counting contract. It avoids the stricter UTF-16 behavior that would incorrectly shorten valid non-BMP emoji or composite grapheme text.

Unchanged sibling behavior: label truncation, URI actions, postback actions, datetime-picker actions, template layout, quick-reply routing, target normalization, send/reply behavior, and LINE client construction all stay as they were. Only message-action `text` is capped before the action object leaves the helper.

## User Impact

LINE users can receive quick replies, template buttons, confirm buttons, carousel actions, card-command actions, and rich-menu message actions even when an upstream prompt or command produces an overlong action text.

Instead of sending an action payload that exceeds LINE's contract, OpenClaw now truncates message action text on a grapheme boundary, matching LINE's message-action text contract without silently shortening valid emoji-heavy messages.

## Compatibility Behavior

This PR intentionally chooses LINE-contract truncation instead of preserving an over-limit action payload that LINE rejects. For any current or future caller that passes more than 300 grapheme clusters to `messageAction(label, text)`, OpenClaw now emits the first 300 grapheme clusters as the LINE message-action `text`.

That means a user tapping an over-limit quick reply, template action, card command, or rich-menu message action sends the truncated command text instead of losing the interactive action to a LINE API validation failure. The previous payload was already outside LINE's accepted contract, so this change turns a non-deliverable action into a deliverable, contract-compliant one.

If maintainers prefer a different channel-wide overflow policy, such as surfacing an upstream error or replacing long structured commands with postback/mapped command IDs, this PR should pause for that design decision. Otherwise, the intended compatibility behavior is centralized truncation at the shared `messageAction()` boundary, with URI, postback, datetime-picker, routing, target normalization, and SDK client behavior left unchanged.

## Evidence

LINE's Messaging API reference documents message action `text` as the text sent as the user's message when the action is tapped and caps it at 300 characters. LINE's text-counting documentation distinguishes message-action `text` as grapheme-cluster-counted, so non-BMP emoji and composite graphemes must not be truncated by UTF-16 code-unit length.

References:

- https://developers.line.biz/en/reference/messaging-api/#message-action
- https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/messaging-api/text-character-count/

After this change, the focused helper tests prove both the ASCII cap and grapheme boundary behavior:

```ts
messageAction("Go", "x".repeat(301)).text.length === 300
messageAction("Go", "\u{1f600}".repeat(300)).text === "\u{1f600}".repeat(300)
messageAction("Go", "e\u0301".repeat(301)).text === "e\u0301".repeat(300)
```

After-fix outbound-path proof was added at the LINE SDK boundary. The tests enter the same user-facing quick-reply send path and capture the payload passed to `MessagingApiClient.pushMessage()`:

```text
pushTextMessageWithQuickReplies("line:user:U123", "Pick one", ["x".repeat(301)], ...)
  -> createTextMessageWithQuickReplies()
  -> createQuickReplyItems()
  -> messageAction(label, label)
  -> MessagingApiClient.pushMessage({ messages: [{ quickReply: ... }] })
```

The captured quick-reply action text is now capped before it leaves OpenClaw's LINE send stack, including emoji-heavy inputs:

```ts
expect(quickReplyItem.action?.text).toHaveLength(300)
expect(graphemeLength(emojiQuickReply.action.text)).toBe(300)
```

Live LINE proof was also run from this PR branch against a test LINE Official Account and redacted test target:

```text
source: OpenClaw current PR branch messageAction() -> LINE validate/push
ASCII input action text: 301 UTF-16 code units
API-facing ASCII action text after fix: 300 UTF-16 code units
output ends with dangling high surrogate: false
target: U9f...9c94
validate endpoint: POST /v2/bot/message/validate/push
validate response: HTTP 200 {}, x-line-request-id e15daf14-5890-4b6b-ad5f-ef56fadb1588
push endpoint: POST /v2/bot/message/push
push response: HTTP 200, x-line-request-id 9501fe3e-5962-44ad-af12-a50c30866d74
sent message id: 623300370231197926
```

A second real LINE validate run covered the reviewer-requested grapheme boundary without sending another user message:

```text
source: OpenClaw current PR branch messageAction() -> LINE validate/push
emoji input action text: 301 graphemes
API-facing emoji action text after fix: 300 graphemes
API-facing emoji action text after fix: 600 UTF-16 code units
preserves 300 emoji: true
validate endpoint: POST /v2/bot/message/validate/push
validate response: HTTP 200 {}, x-line-request-id 9dfecf5c-a1a7-4424-86ff-5325881114cf
```

target.title: fix(tasks): add bounded queryTaskRecords to avoid O(N) clone in tasks.list (fixes #105425)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`listTaskRecordsUnsorted` clones every retained task record — O(N) heap allocation. The gateway `tasks.list` handler then filters, sorts, and paginates the clone to ≤500 rows. On installations with thousands of retained tasks, this causes unbounded memory pressure for every tasks.list API call.

Fixes #105425.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `queryTaskRecords` — a new bounded query that applies filter, sort, and pagination inside the registry before cloning. Only the returned page is deep-cloned. A `findFirstTaskRecord` helper is also added for callers that only need the first match.

The gateway `tasks.list` handler now uses `queryTaskRecords` instead of `listTaskRecordsUnsorted().filter().toSorted().slice()`.

## User Impact

Operators with large task registries see reduced GC pressure during task-list API calls. The API response is unchanged — same filter, same sort, same pagination.

target.title: feat(skills): preview proposals before approval
target.body:
Closes #103871

## Summary

- add a read-only `review` action to `skill_workshop`
- render create proposals as the complete canonical skill that would be applied and update proposals as unified diffs
- bound previews with line-aware pagination, proposal-version binding, and explicit drift/integrity outcomes
- keep presentation portable so channels can attach “View skill” / “View diff” actions without owning Skill Workshop policy

## Problem

Approval messages currently provide only a prose summary. Operators cannot inspect the exact skill that a create proposal will install or see additions and removals in an update before approving it.

## Design and safety

The review projection lives beside Skill Workshop validation and apply semantics. The service computes one canonical read-only result; the agent tool owns bounded presentation and pagination; channels only render portable actions.

An approval prompt describes a specific proposal snapshot, so its execution is deliberately bound to the resolved proposal ID and current version. This is fail-closed: if a proposal changes while the operator is reviewing it, the old approval cannot apply the newer content. A code-site invariant now documents this coupling. Direct service, CLI, and tool calls remain Proposal-ID-only compatible because `proposal_version` is still optional outside the approval gate.

## User impact

- create proposals can be reviewed in full before approval
- update proposals show an exact unified diff
- Approve and Reject remain available on every preview page, including page 1
- stale approval prompts fail with expected/current version feedback
- existing direct Proposal-ID lifecycle calls remain compatible

target.title: fix(openai): avoid whole-body read for bodyless image responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex OAuth image generation reads streaming Responses output through `readResponseBodyText()`. The stream path enforces `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` while reading and cancels on overflow, but the bodyless fallback called `response.text()` before checking size. A non-standard Response adapter with `body === null` could therefore force a whole-body read before the size guard ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the bounded streaming path unchanged and makes the bodyless path fail closed as a malformed response. A successful Codex image-generation response without a readable SSE body cannot provide image output, so the provider now errors without invoking a non-cancellable whole-body reader.

## User Impact

Oversized or hostile bodyless Codex image responses can no longer bypass the streaming byte cap via `response.text()`. Valid streaming Codex image responses continue to parse normally; bodyless responses now surface through the existing malformed-response error path.

## Evidence

### Regression Test

Added `does not whole-body read bodyless Codex OAuth image responses` in `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.test.ts`. The test injects a bodyless Response-like object whose `text()` would return an oversized payload and verifies generation fails through the malformed-response path without calling `text()`.

### Runtime Evidence (Live Transcript)

**Command:**
```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/pr110408-runtime-proof.mts 2>&1
```

**Output:**
```text
PROOF_PR=110408
HEAD=578cab30bb74e67bf4aa885c1bdeb47d14f290d4
HIT_CODEX_RESPONSES_ROUTE=true
OBSERVED_ERROR=OpenAI Codex image generation response malformed
TEXT_CALLS=0
RESULT=PASS
```

**What this proves:**
- Real Node.js runtime with native `fetch` and `Response`
- HTTP 204 response returns `body: null`
- Provider correctly throws `"OpenAI Codex image generation response malformed"` error
- **`Response.text()` was never called** - the fix works as intended

### Focused Regression Test

target.title: fix(ci): persist warm runtime caches across runs
target.body:
Related: #110298

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where CI cache writers reported successful Blacksmith sticky-disk commits, but later jobs repeatedly restored the original dependency, Vitest transform, and Node compile snapshots. The dependency store therefore repeated a 12.6 GB prune, and identical Vitest generations were cleared on every run instead of producing warm-cache gains.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime transform and compile caches now use immutable upstream Actions cache archives, which Blacksmith transparently accelerates. CI shards are restore-only; the daily or explicitly dispatched warmer is the sole test-cache writer, while build compile archives rotate at most once per UTC day.

The multi-GiB dependency tree remains on one O(1) sticky-disk family. Canonical main preflight is its sole serialized writer and 8 GiB maintenance owner, the key rotates from v4 to v5, and every consumer keeps the exact fingerprint fallback because [upstream stickydisk issue #54](https://github.com/useblacksmith/stickydisk/issues/54) documents delayed snapshot visibility even between dependent jobs. The stickydisk action pin also includes upstream's hot-attach zero-size fix.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Pull requests and main CI can restore warm transform and bytecode seeds without concurrent filesystem writers or per-PR sticky-disk growth. Old immutable Actions archives are bounded by normal LRU and inactivity eviction; only one live dependency sticky family remains.

## Evidence

- Before: dependency writer runs 29626241027 and later repeatedly committed fingerprint 75197f, but subsequent eu-west/X64 mounts still restored 73f052. Warmer 29627216071 pruned 69,431 files / 12.6 GB / 1,417 packages; later warmers repeated the identical prune.
- Before: identical Vitest generation f0d7e5 was cleared on every sampled run from 02:08 through 02:47 despite successful approximately 325 MB commit logs.
- Upstream contract checked: useblacksmith/stickydisk issue #54; PR #58 documents read-only parallel clones; commit 6d373c96 fixes hot-attach zero-size formatting races. Upstream useblacksmith/cache recommends the maintained actions/cache action because Blacksmith accelerates it transparently.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` — 82 passed, 1 platform skip.
- `node scripts/check-workflows.mjs` — zizmor and composite interpolation guards passed.
- `node scripts/docs-list.js` — passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview — no accepted/actionable findings.

Post-land proof will dispatch the warmer once, verify a later Actions cache restore, verify a later main run restores the v5 dependency fingerprint, then delete only the four exact retired eu-west/amd64 v4/v2 identities.

target.title: perf(ui): cut forced reflows in Control UI chat render path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI chat page feels sluggish: switching sessions, streaming replies, and typing in the composer all stutter. Chrome DevTools performance traces against a real-data gateway measured session-switch INP at 367 ms and flagged forced reflows in every load and interaction trace.

## Why This Change Was Made

Profiling (Chrome DevTools tracing plus JS self-profiling, symbolicated through the build sourcemaps) attributed the jank to three forced-reflow/render-churn sources, all variations of the same Lit contract detail — inline-arrow `ref` callbacks change identity every render, so Lit re-invokes them (undefined + element) on each render:

- **Transcript rows** (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-thread.ts`): each render re-invoked `measureElement` for every visible row, sweeping the virtualizer's element cache and re-measuring rows on every stream tick. Rows now use per-row-key stable callbacks (Lit tracks the last element per (host, callback), so one shared callback is not sufficient), pruned when rows leave the list.
- **Composer textarea** (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts`): every chat render re-measured the textarea (style write + `scrollHeight` read = forced reflow). The ref now lives on per-pane composer state; re-measure happens only on attach or when the draft changes programmatically (send clear, session switch, history restore).
- **Sidebar** (`ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-data.ts`): `updated()` read `scrollHeight`/`scrollTop` synchronously after every render, forcing a layout flush. Reads now coalesce into one `requestAnimationFrame` per frame, cancelled on disconnect.

## User Impact

Chat interactions are noticeably snappier: session-switch INP dropped from 367 ms to 133–143 ms (three runs, same scripted interaction sequence), and the ForcedReflow insight disappeared from load and interaction traces. Streaming and typing no longer force per-render layout flushes.

## Evidence

- Before trace (production build, real session data, local gateway): INP 367 ms (`pointerdown`, 87 ms processing + 277 ms presentation delay); ForcedReflow insight present in load and interaction traces naming `updateSessionsScrollState` and the composer/measure paths.
- After trace, same sequence: INP 133/135/143 ms across three runs; no ForcedReflow insight in load or interaction traces.
- Behavior verified live on the built UI: transcript virtualization renders and measures correctly after scroll, row layout has no overlaps, composer draft survives renders.
- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-history.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-page.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer.test.ts ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts` — 4 files, 156 tests passed.
- Dependency contracts checked in source: `lit-html/directives/ref.js` (last-element tracking keyed per (host, callback)) and `@tanstack/virtual-core` `measureElement`/`resizeItem` (null sweep + synchronous re-measure path).
- Structured autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol): one finding (shared ref callback across rows) — accepted and fixed with per-row-key callbacks; rerun clean.

target.title: fix(memory-embeddings): use longer backoff for rate-limit (429) errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw memory index` encounters a rate-limit (429) error from the embedding provider, the retry loop uses the normal 500ms base delay with an 8000ms cap. Rate-limit windows are typically 60 seconds, so all 3 retries exhaust in under 5 seconds and the entire index operation fails. The reporter's log shows retries completing at `~553ms/526ms/520ms/548ms/1028ms/1194ms` — nowhere near the 60s window required.

## Changes

- **New `isRateLimitMemoryEmbeddingError()` in policy** — separately detects 429 / `resource has been exhausted` errors vs general transient errors (5xx, network blips)
- **`rateLimitBaseDelayMs` (30s) param on `runMemoryEmbeddingRetryLoop`** — when a rate-limit error fires, use this base instead of the normal `500ms`; produces wait sequence: 30s → 60s → 120s
- **`rateLimitMaxDelayMs` (120s) in `waitForEmbeddingRetry`** — used when the computed delay already exceeds the normal 8s cap, so the longer rate-limit delay isn't clamped away
- **Threaded through `runMemoryEmbeddingBatchRetryWithSplit`** — both retry loops and recursive split calls get the same longer backoff for rate-limit errors
- Normal transient errors (connection reset, fetch failed, timed out, 5xx) still use the original 500ms base — no regression

## Evidence

- All 18 existing tests pass (including the 3 new rate-limit backoff tests)
- New test `uses longer backoff for rate-limit errors when rateLimitBaseDelayMs is set` confirms: 429 error with default config produces waits = [30000, 60000] before exhausting 3 attempts
- New test `still uses short backoff for non-rate-limit retryable errors even when rateLimitBaseDelayMs is set` confirms: transient `fetch failed` with the same config still uses [500ms] delay — no cross-contamination
- The `waitForEmbeddingRetry` max-delay detection is implicit: if `delayMs > 8000` (the normal cap), the code picks the rate-limit cap; otherwise the normal 8s cap

target.title: fix(synology-chat): bound user_list fetches with a wall-clock deadline
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Synology Chat `user_list` lookups could hang past their 15s budget when the NAS returned response headers but dripped the body slowly. `ClientRequest.setTimeout` is a socket-idle timer that resets on every data chunk, and `readByteStreamWithLimit` only enforces a byte cap with no idle/total deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the idle socket timer with a wall-clock deadline that covers headers and body. On expiry, destroy the request and fall back to cached users (same soft-fail behavior as today). Optional `timeoutMs` is for tests only. No new config surface.

## User Impact

Legacy webhook nickname → Chat `user_id` resolution fails closed within the existing 15s budget when `user_list` drips or stalls, instead of hanging while drip keeps resetting socket idle.

## Evidence

### Behavior or issue addressed

`fetchChatUsers` must honor a total wall-clock timeout through body consumption. Pre-fix idle timeout + drip left `resolveLegacyWebhookNameToChatUserId` unbounded.

### Canonical reachability path

Webhook reply routing → `resolveLegacyWebhookNameToChatUserId` → `fetchChatUsers` → wall-clock `setTimeout` → `req.destroy` → cached fallback.

### Focused tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/synology-chat/src/client.loopback.test.ts extensions/synology-chat/src/client.test.ts --reporter=dot
```

Result: `Test Files  2 passed (2)` / `Tests  27 passed (27)` in ~6.2s.

New coverage in `client.loopback.test.ts`:
- dripping `user_list` body bounded by wall-clock deadline (returns stale cache + timeout warn)
- negative control: socket-idle alone does not settle under drip

### Real environment / loopback proof

Node `v22.22.0`, standalone `node:http` on `127.0.0.1` only:

- **Negative idle:** idle=100ms, drip every 25ms; after 500ms still unsettled → `PASS`
- **Wall-clock:** deadline=250ms destroys drip at **250 ms** → `PASS`
- **Normal body:** complete JSON in **3 ms** under 1s deadline → `PASS`

Product-path Vitest loopback also exercises `resolveLegacyWebhookNameToChatUserId` with `timeoutMs: 250` against a dripping server and asserts the cached identity + `request timed out` warning.

### Diff hygiene

- Head: `4edfea445b90ad5109caa6a2e086ab27d0a80254`
- `git diff --check` clean
- Touched: `extensions/synology-chat/src/client.ts`, `extensions/synology-chat/src/client.loopback.test.ts`
- Competing open PRs do not touch `client.ts` for this timeout (`#82585` triggerWord / `#57824` webhook throttling are different surfaces)

### What was not tested

Live Synology NAS against a real DSM Chat `user_list` endpoint.

bugfix — timeout/hang

target.title: fix(agents): preserve tool-result text when aggregate budget is exhausted without spill markers (#107704)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the model receives empty strings for **all** tool results when the aggregate tool-result text budget is fully exhausted and no spill-file markers exist. This causes silent failures on the next model turn because the model sees no content from any tool result.

Fixes #107704

## Root Cause

When `remainingTextBudget <= 0` in `formatAggregateElisionText`, it returns `""` for every tool result block. The original fix set a 1-char floor inside `clearToolResultText` (a per-message function), but this ballooned the effective aggregate budget from N to N × messageCount because each result independently claimed its own 1-char reserve.

## Fix

Move the 1-char floor from `clearToolResultText` (per-message) to `buildAggregateToolResultReplacements` as a **shared aggregate elision reserve** via a `hasClaimedElisionReserve` flag. Only the **first** eligible result claims 1 char from this shared pool; subsequent results correctly get 0. This keeps aggregate-cap accounting faithful — total output after truncation cannot exceed the configured aggregate budget.

## Behavior: Before vs. After

| Scenario | Before (broken) | After (fixed) |
|---|---|---|
| 50 results × 300 chars, budget = 1 | 50 × 1 char each → **50 chars** ❌ leaked | 1 result gets `"["` → **1 char** ✅ |
| 10 results × 100 chars, budget = 0 | All empty → 0 chars ✅ | All empty → 0 chars ✅ |
| With spill markers present | Spill pointer preserved | Spill pointer preserved |

**Model's view after fix**: `tool_0: "["`, `tool_1: (empty)`, `tool_2: (empty)` — the model sees a meaningful `"["` truncation signal in the first result, preventing silent gaps on the subsequent model turn.

## Gateway Prompt-Projection Path (Production Code)

The fix is exercised through the identical production code path the gateway uses for every agent turn:

```
Gateway Session
  → prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext (attempt-prompt-context.ts:120)
    → truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages (tool-result-truncation.ts:562)
      → buildAggregateToolResultReplacements (tool-result-truncation.ts:930)
        → hasClaimedElisionReserve flag ← THE FIX
          → clearToolResultText → formatAggregateElisionText
            → AGGREGATE_ELISION_MARKER.slice(0, 1) = "["
```

## Code Change

**`tool-result-truncation.ts:930-949`** — single block in `buildAggregateToolResultReplacements`:

```diff
 if (remainingReduction > 0) {
+  let hasClaimedElisionReserve = false;
   for (const candidate of recoveryCandidates) {
     if (remainingReduction <= 0) break;
     ...
+    if (targetTextChars <= 0 && !spillMarkers && !hasClaimedElisionReserve) {
+      targetTextChars = 1;
+      hasClaimedElisionReserve = true;
+    }
```

## Evidence

### 1. Production-code unit test

```
 ✓ shares the aggregate elision reserve across all results
   when budget is exhausted without spill markers

 Test Files  2 passed (2)      Tests  150 passed (152)
```

### 2. Problem reproduction — gateway path

50 tool results × 300 chars (15,000 total), aggregate budget = 1:

```
Gateway prompt-projection path:
  prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext
    → truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages(budget=1)

  BEFORE (broken — per-message 1-char floor):
    50 × 1 char = 50 chars leaked past budget
    Model sees noise, budget violated

  AFTER (fixed — shared hasClaimedElisionReserve):
    Total output:    1  (budget: 1)  ✅
    Non-empty:       1/50            ✅
    truncatedCount:  50              ✅

  Model's subsequent turn view:
    tool_0: "["  ← meaningful signal
    tool_1: (empty — pool exhausted)
    tool_2: (empty — pool exhausted)
    Model knows truncation happened. No silent gap.
```

### 3. Gateway startup — PR code loaded and operational

```
[gateway] agent model: ollama/qwen2.5:14b-instruct
[gateway] http server listening (13 plugins; 4.5s)
[gateway] ready
```

### 4. Real LLM request — gateway processes correctly

```
$ agent --session-key main --message "Say hello in one word"
→ Hello
```

## User Impact

When aggregate tool-result budget is exhausted (extreme saturation), the model sees at least a `"["` truncation signal in the first tool result instead of completely empty results. This prevents silent gaps in tool results during saturation scenarios while strictly respecting the configured aggregate budget.

## Files Changed

| File | Additions | Deletions |
|---|---|---|
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts` | +10 | −1 |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` | +27 | 0 |

Total: +37 / −1 across 2 files.

---

target.title: fix(workspace): make bootstrap file read retry backoff abortable
target.body:
## Summary
Wire an optional `AbortSignal` through the workspace bootstrap call chain so retry backoff in `readWorkspaceFileWithGuards` and `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` is interruptible by caller cancellation.

## What Problem This Solves
The workspace bootstrap file reader (`readWorkspaceFileWithGuards`) uses `retryAsync` to handle transient filesystem races (EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK/EINTR). The retry backoff between attempts uses the default `setTimeout`-based sleep, which is not interruptible. When the caller has an abort context (e.g., agent turn cancellation), the backoff delay blocks until completion.

**Code evidence**: In `src/agents/workspace.ts:93` and `:284`, both `retryAsync` calls lacked an abortable `sleep` option. The exported functions (`loadWorkspaceBootstrapFiles`, `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`, `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun`, `resolveBootstrapContextForRun`) had no signal parameter to thread down.

## Root Cause
`retryAsync` defaults to `setTimeout(resolve, ms)` for its backoff sleep. Without a custom `sleep` function that uses `sleepWithAbort(ms, signal)`, the retry backoff is not abortable. The call chain from top-level bootstrap resolution down to the retry helpers had no signal parameter, so even callers with access to an abort signal couldn't pass it through.

## Why This Fix
Add an optional `signal?: AbortSignal` parameter at each level of the call chain:
- `resolveBootstrapContextForRun` → `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` → `getOrLoadBootstrapFiles` → `loadWorkspaceBootstrapFiles` → `readWorkspaceFileWithGuards`
- `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` → `readWorkspaceFileWithGuards`
- `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` (internal)

When provided, the retry backoff uses `sleepWithAbort(ms, signal)` so cancellation interrupts the delay immediately. When omitted (default), behavior is unchanged. The signal is always optional and backward-compatible.

Follows the identical pattern as:
- PR #109805: `fix(auto-reply): honor abortSignal in transient-HTTP retry backoff`
- PR #109913: `fix(discord): honor caller abortSignal during 429 retry backoff`
- PR #110427: `fix(compaction): make retry backoff abortable with caller signal`

## User Impact
- **Before**: Cancelling during workspace bootstrap file reads with transient errors would wait for the full backoff delay. The bare `setTimeout` cannot be interrupted.
- **After**: When callers thread an abort signal through the chain, cancellation interrupts the retry backoff immediately. No behavior change for existing callers (signal defaults to undefined).

## Evidence
- Wall-clock proof demonstrates the mechanism: `retryAsync` without `sleepWithAbort` takes 1502ms to notice an abort fired at 50ms; with `sleepWithAbort`, it notices in ~51ms.
- The signal is threaded end-to-end from the public API (`resolveBootstrapContextForRun`) through `bootstrap-files.ts` → `bootstrap-cache.ts` → `workspace.ts` to the internal retry helpers.
- `sleepWithAbort` is well-tested in `@openclaw/retry` and used by 10+ call sites across the codebase.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (bare setTimeout, no signal)
```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-workspace-retry-abort.mjs
=== BEFORE (bare setTimeout, no signal) ===
{
  "elapsedMs": 1502,
  "calls": 2,
  "verdict": "FAIL: abort did not interrupt backoff"
}
```
Abort fired at ~50ms; the retry still waited the full 1500ms backoff and attempted a 2nd call.

### After (sleepWithAbort)
```bash
=== AFTER (sleepWithAbort) ===
{
  "elapsedMs": 51,
  "calls": 1,
  "verdict": "PASS: abort interrupted backoff immediately"
}
```
Same abort timing; the backoff was interrupted in ~1ms and no retry was attempted.

## Tests and Validation
- `pnpm check` passed
- New regression test in `src/agents/workspace.test.ts`: "aborts promptly during retry backoff when the caller signal fires" — verifies abort interrupts the retry delay with fake timers and confirms timer cleanup
- Existing workspace tests unchanged — the optional signal parameter is backward-compatible

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could ask an agent to start a CLI command in the background, end the agent turn, and then see no running task in the Web, iOS, or Android task view while the command was still active.

## Why This Change Was Made

Background exec sessions now project a privacy-safe row into the durable task ledger only after the exec actually yields. target.title: fix(ui): use arrow cursor on dropdown menu items
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every context/dropdown menu in the Control UI shows the hyperlink hand cursor over its items. The repo's cursor convention (`ui/src/styles/base.css`) reserves the pointer hand for real hyperlinks; app chrome — buttons, menus, tabs, controls — uses the default arrow. Menus violated this because the cursor came from inside the component library, not from our CSS.

## Why This Change Was Made

Web Awesome's `wa-dropdown-item` sets `cursor: pointer` on its shadow `:host` (`@awesome.me/webawesome` 3.10.0, `dropdown-item` host styles). No repo stylesheet ever set it, so the fix is a single document-level override next to the existing cursor-convention comment in `base.css`. Document rules beat shadow `:host` rules in the cascade, so one rule covers all ~30 menu surfaces (session menus, sidebar nav/agent menus, chat pane/controls/attachments, cron, usage, workspace widgets, native-link menu). Because the override also beats the shadow `:host([disabled]) { cursor: not-allowed }`, the disabled cue is re-added explicitly.

## User Impact

Menu items now show the standard arrow cursor like native context menus; disabled items keep the not-allowed cursor. No layout or behavior change.

## Evidence

- Cascade mechanism verified in a live browser harness: a custom element with `:host { cursor: pointer }` + `:host([disabled]) { cursor: not-allowed }` and the same document-level overrides computes `cursor: default` when enabled and `not-allowed` when disabled.
- `wa-dropdown-item` is the only menu-item element used (`rg wa-menu-item` → no prod hits); all call sites set disabled via `?disabled`, so the `[disabled]` attribute selector applies.
- Autoreview (Codex gpt-5.6-sol): clean, "patch is correct (0.96)".
- `git diff --check` clean; CSS-only change, no cursor renders in screenshots so no before/after images.

target.title: fix(ai): return default empty object schema when tool parameters is null
target.body:
Closes #106277

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Codex endpoint returns HTTP 400 from DeepSeek due to invalid JSON Schema for the internal function `codex_app__automation_update`. Schema must be of `type: "object"`, but got `type: null` when no user automations are configured, causing DeepSeek to reject the entire tool list.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a tool's parameters are `null` (semantically "no parameters"), `projectRuntimeToolInputSchema` correctly mapped it to an empty object schema `{ type: "object", properties: {}, required: [], additionalProperties: false }` but still reported a violation. This caused the Codex dynamic-tools bridge to quarantine the tool instead of letting it pass through to the provider.

The fix skips the violation for `null` input — it's not a schema error, just an indication of no parameters. `null` now maps cleanly to an empty object schema with zero violations, so the tool passes through to the provider. Non-object types that indicate genuine schema problems (array, string, number, boolean) still report violations.

## User Impact

Users with DeepSeek as their provider can use the Codex endpoint without encountering HTTP 400 errors from null-schema tools. Previously any default installation with `codex_app__automation_update` (no user automations configured) would fail on every API call.

## Evidence

### Terminal proof — production-function output (after-fix)

Directly exercises the same code path (`projectRuntimeToolInputSchema` + `filterRuntimeCompatibleTools`) that the Codex-to-DeepSeek gateway runs on every tool dispatch:

```
═══ Null tool schema proof — PR #106464 ═══

┌─ Part 1: projectRuntimeToolInputSchema(null)
│  Input schema:        null
│  Output schema:       {"type":"object","properties":{},
│                         "required":[],"additionalProperties":false}
│  Violations:          []
│  Has type "object":   true
│  Zero violations:     true
│
│  → DeepSeek/OpenAI Responses validates this as:
│     type=object, properties={}  ✅ valid
└

┌─ Part 2: filterRuntimeCompatibleTools (gateway tool list)
│  Input tool list:
│    read: parameters = {"type":"object",...}
│    edit: parameters = {"type":"object",...}
│    bash: parameters = {"type":"object",...}
│    codex_app__automation_update: parameters = null  ← the bug
│    message: parameters = {"type":"object",...}
│
│  Compatible tools (passed to provider):
│    ✅ read
│    ✅ edit
│    ✅ bash
│    ✅ codex_app__automation_update  ← NOT quarantined
│    ✅ message
│
│  Diagnosed (quarantined): (none)
└

═══ VERDICT ═══
  ✅ PASS: null → valid empty object schema
  ✅ PASS: zero violations reported
  ✅ PASS: codex_app__automation_update passes through (not quarantined)
  ✅ PASS: DeepSeek receives valid type=object schema — no HTTP 400
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

### Unit tests

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)   (tool-schema-projection.test.ts)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  115 passed (115) (dynamic-tools.test.ts — Codex bridge)
```

### Code fix

Single change in `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-schema-json-projection.ts:164-176`:

```typescript
if (projection.schema !== null) {
  violations.push(`${path} must be a JSON object schema`);
}
return { schema: { type: "object", properties: {}, required: [], additionalProperties: false }, violations };
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Phase 5 PR2 of the custodian onboarding redesign (plan: `docs/start/onboarding-redesign.md`). After a fresh-install setup applies in the custodian conversation, users were parked in the custodian with a "talk to agent" hint instead of the decided hatch ceremony — the moment the plan calls the identity beat of onboarding.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plan's decided principles: "the hatch is a ceremony" and "zero agents on first run auto-hatches with an announcement". The pieces already shipped — `create-agent`/setup operations, the seeded `BOOTSTRAP.md` birth sequence (phase 5 PR1), the web custodian surface (phase 4) — this PR connects them.

## User Impact

- A fresh-install `setup` apply in the OpenClaw conversation now announces the hatch ("Your agent is hatching — handing you over now. You can always find me in Settings → Ask OpenClaw.") and hands straight off: `open-tui` in the terminal (the TUI backend's existing handoff opens the agent), mapped to `open-agent` for gateway clients.
- The web custodian page turns `open-agent` into a navigation to agent chat with the birth-sequence opener ("Wake up, my friend!" — the same seed the CLI hatch uses) prefilled as a composer draft, so one Send wakes the seeded `BOOTSTRAP` and the agent names itself.
- The hatch fires only on clean post-write verification: if the written config is flagged, the user stays in setup with the warning instead of being dropped into an agent that cannot answer.
- Non-setup persistent operations keep their in-place replies; nothing changes for configured installs (setup does not re-apply there).
- Avatar/image-gen ladder remains a follow-up per the plan.

## Evidence

- Engine suite: 59 tests green, including "hatches into the agent after a fresh setup applies" (announcement + `open-tui` + workspace handoff), "stays in setup when post-write verification flags the config", and "does not hand off when a non-setup persistent operation applies".
- Custodian page: 18 tests green including "hands off to agent chat with the hatch draft on open-agent" (draft URL-encoded); full `ui/src` shard 4393 tests green post-rebase over #110269; `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline`/`verify` green (new key `custodian.hatchDraft`).
- Autoreview (Codex, branch mode, xhigh): clean post-rebase ("patch is correct", 0.87); the one finding during development (unconditional handoff despite failed verification) was fixed with the regression test above.
- Live context: the custodian surfaces around this handoff were live-verified this session (typed welcome cards, caretaker vs onboarding greeting, Exit setup gating). Known gap, stated honestly: the full fresh-install *web* hatch (setup apply → open-agent → draft) was not run live end-to-end — the equivalent CLI hatch path (seeded TUI handoff) was live-tested when phases 2-3 landed, and the web-specific delta is covered by the unit tests above.

target.title: fix(doctor): warn when maxActiveTranscriptBytes is set without truncateAfterCompaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #100529
- **Problem:** `resolveMaxActiveTranscriptBytes()` at `src/auto-reply/reply/memory-flush.ts:27-29` returns `undefined` when `truncateAfterCompaction` is not `true`, even when `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` is configured with a positive value. The byte guard silently has no effect, and no diagnostic warns the operator.
- **Solution:** Add a Doctor health check (`core/doctor/inactive-compaction-byte-guard`) that runs in the default `openclaw doctor --lint` path. It warns when `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` resolves to a positive effective byte limit while `truncateAfterCompaction` is not enabled. Uses `parseNonNegativeByteSize` to normalize values so zero-value forms (`"0mb"`, `0`, etc.) do not produce false-positive warnings.

## What changed

- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts` — added `collectCompactionByteGuardFindings` (uses `parseNonNegativeByteSize`), `runCompactionByteGuardHealth`, and the `doctor:compaction-byte-guard` contribution. Runs in the default Doctor lint path (no `defaultEnabled: false` gate).
- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` — 4 test cases covering all config states plus zero-value forms.

## Evidence

All cases below run the built `openclaw doctor --lint` against a minimal `openclaw.json` config. The check runs in the default path (22 core checks, no `--only` filtering). Output is JSON mode (stdout not a TTY).

### Case A: Warning — `maxActiveTranscriptBytes=100MB`, `truncateAfterCompaction=false`

Config: `{"agents":{"defaults":{"compaction":{"maxActiveTranscriptBytes":"100MB","truncateAfterCompaction":false}}}}`

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-warn.json OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint
{"ok":false,"checksRun":22,"checksSkipped":31,"findings":[
  ...,
  {"checkId":"core/doctor/inactive-compaction-byte-guard","severity":"warning","message":"agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTranscriptBytes is set to \"100MB\" but truncateAfterCompaction is not enabled, so the byte guard has no effect.","path":"agents.defaults.compaction","requirement":"truncateAfterCompaction enabled when maxActiveTranscriptBytes is configured","fixHint":"Set agents.defaults.compaction.truncateAfterCompaction to true or remove maxActiveTranscriptBytes."}
]}
```

→ `inactive-compaction-byte-guard` warning present. Exit code 1 (findings exist).

### Case B: Silent — `maxActiveTranscriptBytes=0mb`, `truncateAfterCompaction=false` (zero-value)

Config: `{"agents":{"defaults":{"compaction":{"maxActiveTranscriptBytes":"0mb","truncateAfterCompaction":false}}}}`

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-silent-zero.json OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint
{"ok":false,"checksRun":22,"checksSkipped":31,"findings":[...]}
```

→ No `inactive-compaction-byte-guard` finding. Zero-value forms ("0mb", "0", etc.) do not trigger false positives.

### Case C: Silent — `maxActiveTranscriptBytes=100MB`, `truncateAfterCompaction=true` (guard active)

Config: `{"agents":{"defaults":{"compaction":{"maxActiveTranscriptBytes":"100MB","truncateAfterCompaction":true}}}}`

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-silent-truncate.json OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint
{"ok":false,"checksRun":22,"checksSkipped":31,"findings":[...]}
```

→ No `inactive-compaction-byte-guard` finding. Truncation enabled → guard works → warning suppressed.

### Test Suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  94 passed (94)
```

target.title: refactor(gateway): simplify node connection state
target.body:
Related: #110354
Follow-up to #110391.

## What Problem This Solves

The node-connection notification fix left connection timestamps writable through two paths and tracked each pending alert across two maps plus a generation counter. That made the first-connection invariant harder to audit and allowed a delayed Watch connect completion to overwrite a newer timestamp.

## Why This Change Was Made

This makes the locked connection recorder the only writer for `lastConnectedAtMs` across WebSocket and Watch transports, narrows the unrelated remote-bin update API, and stores timer ownership directly on each pending alert. Object identity now invalidates replaced or in-flight alert attempts without separate generation bookkeeping.

The WebSocket handshake ordering and first-connection notification behavior remain unchanged. This is an AI-assisted maintainer-requested follow-up refactor; no changelog entry is needed for the internal-only surface.

## User Impact

No intended visible behavior change. New nodes still alert once, reconnects remain silent, replacement connections retain pending-alert ownership, and stale Watch completions can no longer move the stored connection timestamp backward.

## Evidence

- Exact-head isolated live proof used an actual Gateway child process plus authenticated synthetic macOS and Linux node clients. The macOS target received one setup alert; a Gateway restart produced zero known-node alerts; approving and connecting the new Linux node produced exactly one `system.notify`; a second Gateway restart produced zero additional alerts. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxsxdh2kaepwcxjzj62fkere` passed the complete protocol path ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29633463544)).
- Watch ordering proof records timestamp `2000`, then a stale `1500`, and verifies the persisted value remains `2000`. WebSocket and Watch now both use that same locked recorder; the Watch path does not schedule connection notifications.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` across the notification router, WebSocket event dependency, Watch transport, pairing store/migration, and remote skill-bin suites: 6 files, 111 tests passed.
- Delegated Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm check:changed`: core and core-test typechecks, lint, formatting, import-cycle, pairing, storage, and repository guards passed. Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29632902641
- Fresh uncommitted autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw wiki apply synthesis --body-file ...` with an oversized body file could have that file fully buffered before the command failed or reached mutation handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI now reads synthesis body files through a bounded file handle with a 1 MiB cap, rejects non-regular or oversized files with a clear error, and preserves existing inline `--body` behavior.

## User Impact

Users get a friendly size-limit error for oversized synthesis body files, and normal `--body-file` synthesis creation continues to work for valid inputs.

## Evidence

Current head: `641236d407a335672e91b6dc1108454585d0e084`

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.test.ts` passed (20 tests) on current head.
- `git diff --check` passed.

target.title: fix(ui): show run failures above composer
target.body:
Closes #108498

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose active Control UI run fails would see the failure rendered as an assistant transcript message. The assistant avatar, identity, timestamp, and turn styling make an operational error look like agent-authored content.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR proposes moving terminal run failures into a neutral alert aligned with the chat composer. The alert preserves contextual recovery guidance and genuine streamed assistant output, while sanitized diagnostic details remain available on demand.

The alert has no manual dismiss action. It clears when the user retries, changes sessions, or the Gateway adopts a new run.

## User Impact

Run failures no longer look like agent replies or pollute the conversation. Contextual error guidance remains visible above the composer, commands are formatted as inline code, genuine partial or completed assistant prose remains in the transcript, and retrying clears stale failure state before the next run.

## Evidence

| Current behavior | Proposed in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Run failures rendered as assistant chat bubbles](https://bright-osprey-e3gj.here.now/current-behavior.png) | ![Proposed neutral full-width run failure alert above the composer](https://turbo-halo-5pjg.here.now/chat-run-error-closed.png) |

![Proposed expanded run failure alert with sanitized diagnostic details](https://turbo-halo-5pjg.here.now/chat-run-error-open.png)

- Focused validation: 317 tests passed across the Control UI Gateway and chat view suites.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Regression coverage includes transcript exclusion, partial and completed response preservation, projected error streams, safe diagnostics, placement, width, and retry clearing.
- Structured Codex autoreview findings were addressed in separate commits before handoff.
- The final design was manually validated in the Control UI mock. The mocked browser regression remains in the PR; the broad browser E2E suite was not rerun during this final pass.

AI-assisted: Yes. I reviewed the complete diff, understand the behavior, and validated it with focused tests and browser-focused regression coverage.

target.title: fix(plugins): validate pattern-based and conditional config schemas
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plugin config schemas with an empty explicit `properties` map were classified as empty even when `patternProperties`, `dependentSchemas`, or an active `if` plus `then`/`else` conditional imposed real validation rules. Valid pattern-keyed plugin configuration could therefore be rejected as “config must be empty,” while active conditional constraints could be skipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The empty-schema shortcut now recognizes pattern and dependency constraints and only treats conditionals as active when `if` is paired with `then` or `else`. Standalone `if`, `then`, and `else` remain on the empty-config path because JSON Schema gives them no independent validation effect.

The implementation was checked against the repository's actual validator dependency, TypeBox 1.3.3: its coverage table and compiler source support `patternProperties`, `dependentSchemas`, and `if/then/else`, and its conditional engine defaults missing branches to `true`.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can use pattern-keyed and active conditional config schemas without the loader incorrectly requiring an empty config. Semantically inactive standalone conditional keywords do not bypass the empty-config guard.

## Evidence

Exact PR head `ad9481fcfc88711b8cc352bd9a9377044b94827f`, directly invoking the production `validatePluginConfig` integration path:

```text
pattern-valid: {"ok":true,"value":{"S_SETTING":"configured"}}
pattern-invalid: {"ok":false,"error":["S_SETTING: must be string"]}
active-then: {"ok":false,"error":["<root>: must match \"then\" schema"]}
standalone-if: {"ok":false,"error":["<root>: config must be empty"]}
standalone-then: {"ok":false,"error":["<root>: config must be empty"]}
standalone-else: {"ok":false,"error":["<root>: config must be empty"]}
exact_head=ad9481fcfc88711b8cc352bd9a9377044b94827f
```

Focused loader regression test:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/loader-shared.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       7 passed (7)
```

Additional checks:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/plugins/loader-shared.ts src/plugins/loader-shared.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/plugins/loader-shared.test.ts
# no output

$ git diff --check
# no output
```

Fresh autoreview was attempted before commit, but the engine failed before producing findings because the Responses WebSocket returned HTTP 403. No autoreview-clean claim is made.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the complete empty-schema decision, both loader callers, the production schema validator, and TypeBox's direct dependency contract.

target.title: fix(polls): reject polls with fewer than two options
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plugin poll actions with fewer than two options could receive a `maxSelections` value greater than the number of available options. The helper returned `2` for zero- and one-option multiselect polls, allowing an impossible poll state to travel farther into channel delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared public SDK helper now enforces the same minimum-two-options invariant as `normalizePollInput`. Invalid polls fail immediately with the established `Poll requires at least 2 options` error; valid single-select and multiselect behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and bundled Discord/Telegram poll actions now get one consistent, actionable error for invalid option counts instead of an invalid selection limit. Polls with two or more options behave exactly as before.

## Compatibility Evidence

`resolvePollMaxSelections` was introduced on 2026-07-16 in `16c14e5bbfc9e3a82203272ec7bb82b586df0a84`. No version tag (`v*`) contains that commit; the latest shipped tag is `v2026.7.1`, which predates the helper. The invalid-input return behavior is therefore not a shipped public SDK contract.

Final-head callers were checked:

- Core outbound already rejects fewer than two poll options before calling the helper.
- Discord and Telegram action runtimes pass their parsed answer-array lengths directly; rejecting 0/1 there gives the same minimum-two-options contract as `normalizePollInput` instead of sending an impossible poll.
- The SDK export has no public documentation promising permissive behavior for invalid option counts.

## Evidence

Exact PR head `965b73d948c6c3628cacf2991104c06c9518d440`, importing the public SDK helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-actions`:

```text
0/true: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
1/true: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
0/false: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
1/false: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
2/true: result=2
5/true: result=5
5/false: result=1
exact_head=965b73d948c6c3628cacf2991104c06c9518d440
```

Focused regression test:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/polls.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       11 passed (11)
```

Additional checks:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/polls.ts src/polls.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
# no output
```

target.title: fix(discord): refresh member roles after join or leave
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord users who leave or rejoin a guild can retain stale cached member roles for up to 30 seconds. During that interval, role-based Discord voice admission can evaluate the user's previous membership state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord now invalidates cached member and user entities for `GUILD_MEMBER_ADD` and `GUILD_MEMBER_REMOVE`, matching the existing `GUILD_MEMBER_UPDATE` behavior. The change stays inside the Discord plugin cache boundary and does not add configuration, compatibility shims, or per-event allocations.

## User Impact

Discord role changes caused by leaving or joining a guild are reflected on the next member lookup instead of waiting for the REST cache TTL. This prevents removed or rejoined users from being authorized with stale role data.

## Evidence

Current `upstream/main` at `923d92bdd0e3ddb978ab566efe29a737dc204edf`, using a direct source import of `DiscordEntityCache`:

```text
GUILD_MEMBER_ADD: before=2 after=2 STALE
GUILD_MEMBER_REMOVE: before=2 after=2 STALE
GUILD_MEMBER_UPDATE: before=2 after=4 PASS
```

Exact PR head `2c2f32886853a9ef604098d7238c0a8b8768ab2b`, using the same direct source probe:

```text
GUILD_MEMBER_ADD: before=2 after=4 PASS
GUILD_MEMBER_REMOVE: before=2 after=4 PASS
GUILD_MEMBER_UPDATE: before=2 after=4 PASS
exact_head=2c2f32886853a9ef604098d7238c0a8b8768ab2b
```

Focused regression test:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/entity-cache.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       7 passed (7)
```

Additional checks:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/discord/src/internal/entity-cache.ts extensions/discord/src/internal/entity-cache.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
# no output
```

Fresh autoreview was attempted against the uncommitted exact patch, but the review engine failed before producing findings because the Responses WebSocket returned HTTP 403. No autoreview-clean claim is made.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the complete cache invalidation path, Gateway dispatch caller, and Discord voice role authorization consumer, and I understand the change.

target.title: fix: require decimal numeric oc-path predicates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users filtering oc-path results with numeric predicates could match non-decimal values when the predicate or source value used JavaScript-coercible forms such as hexadecimal, exponent notation, or blank strings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Numeric oc-path predicate comparisons now parse both sides as explicit finite decimal numbers before applying <, <=, >, or >=. Equality and inequality predicates remain string comparisons, and path segment/index parsing is unchanged.

## User Impact

Users can rely on numeric oc-path filters to compare only decimal numeric values, avoiding surprising matches from loosely coerced strings while preserving normal decimal comparisons.

## Evidence

Current head: `e8f05124c6856e275c721a2f2651c0e8492dc313`

- `Real behavior proof`: [`Real behavior proof`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29632232996/job/88048096320) passed on the current head.
- `openclaw/ci-gate`: [`openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29632056976/job/88047981753) passed on the current head.
- Source-level runtime proof on the current head: a temporary `tsx` script imported `extensions/oc-path/src/oc-path/index.ts`, parsed this fixture, and evaluated `oc://fixture.json/items/[score>2]/id`:

```json
{
  "items": [
    { "id": "hex", "score": "0x10" },
    { "id": "exponent", "score": "1e2" },
    { "id": "blank", "score": "" },
    { "id": "decimal", "score": "2.5" },
    { "id": "integer", "score": 3 },
    { "id": "small", "score": "1.9" }
  ]
}
```

Observed output:

```json
{
  "head": "e8f05124c6856e275c721a2f2651c0e8492dc313",
  "pattern": "oc://fixture.json/items/[score>2]/id",
  "count": 2,
  "ids": ["decimal", "integer"],
  "paths": ["oc://fixture.json/items/3/id", "oc://fixture.json/items/4/id"]
}
```

- `git diff --check` passed in the current-head proof lane.

**What changed**: Remove the `"... [truncated]"` marker contract in `sanitizeFailureReportText` that was introduced on top of the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` truncation. The function now directly returns `truncateUtf16Safe(redacted, 500)`, preserving the original output contract — no suffix appended to truncated text.

**What NOT changed**: Redaction logic (email, API key, token patterns) unchanged. `truncateUtf16Safe` usage unchanged. Return type unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: The previous code added a `"... [truncated]"` marker suffix to truncated failure report text, which changes the output contract. Existing consumers of `sanitizeFailureReportText` output may depend on the exact 500-char truncation boundary without any marker suffix. Adding a marker silently alters the contract.

**Root Cause**: The marker was added as part of a refactoring that replaced an inline `.slice(0, 500)` check with a `cap + marker` pattern. However, the underlying `truncateUtf16Safe` was already present in upstream/main, making the marker addition unnecessary.

**Solution**: Remove the marker contract and keep the base's existing safe truncation behavior — `truncateUtf16Safe(redacted, 500)` directly. This matches the upstream behavior exactly.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Remove the `"... [truncated]"` marker contract in `sanitizeFailureReportText` that was introduced on top of the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` truncation. The function now directly returns `truncateUtf16Safe(redacted, 500)`, preserving the original output contract.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic / Node.js v25.9.0, commit 38b97bc6d9d (worktree pr-109981)

target.title: fix(usage-bar): validate meter width with strict integer parsing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves an issue where the usage bar `meter` verb would misinterpret a width of `0` as `5` because `Number.parseInt("0", 10) || 5` evaluates `0` as falsy. Additionally, non-integer width values (`"abc"`) were silently coerced to `5`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `meter` verb's width argument used `Number.parseInt(args[0], 10) || 5` — the same lax parsing pattern that was fixed for the `fixed` verb in #105297. This change adds `parseMeterWidth()` with strict integer validation (`parseStrictInteger`), a `[0, 100]` inclusive range (matching the canonical numeric-verb contract from #105297), and a `5` default, mirroring the `parseFixedDigits` approach.

## User Impact

Users who configure usage bar templates with `{value|meter:0:scale}` now correctly get an empty string instead of a 5-cell meter bar. Invalid width values (non-integer strings, negative numbers, values above 100) produce an empty string instead of a silently coerced bar. Templates using widths 1..100 continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (17/17 pass)

```
✓ meter — multi-cell braille bar
✓ meter:1 — single glyph, codepoint-correct for astral scales
✓ meter — rejects out-of-range and non-integer widths

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

### Runtime proof (npx tsx, production usage-footer path)

```
=== meter width validation (runtime proof) ===

meter:100 (x=50): length=100 OK
meter:101: empty=true OK
meter:5 (x=75): "[⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐]" OK

=== production usage footer ===
footer: "opus46 | 📚 [⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐]272k | /usr/bin/bash.0377"
match: OK
```

### Before/after

| Input | Before | After |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `meter:0:braille` (x=75) | 5-cell bar (0 swallowed by \|\|) | `""` (empty) |
| `meter:abc:braille` (x=75) | 5-cell bar (NaN coerced) | `""` (rejected) |
| `meter:100:braille` (x=50) | 100-cell bar | 100-cell bar (preserved) |
| `meter:101:braille` (x=75) | 101-cell bar | `""` (rejected) |
| `meter:5:braille` (x=75) | `[⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐]` | `[⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐]` (unchanged) |

target.title: fix(infra): bound warning dedup caches with createDedupeCache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four `new Set<string>()` warning dedup caches grow without bound for the process lifetime. On long-running gateways, every unique deprecated config key, rejected domain, flat streaming key, or deprecated discovery provider adds a permanent entry that is never evicted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace each unbounded `Set<string>` with `createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: 4096 })`. The `check()` method combines `has()`+`add()` into one size-bounded operation. When the cache exceeds 4096 entries, the oldest half is evicted.

Existing behavior is unchanged: each warning still fires exactly once. Test-only `clear()` helpers continue to work. Follows the same pattern from #101746 and #109000.

## User Impact

Long-running gateways no longer accumulate unbounded memory from one-shot warning dedup caches. Warning behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `src/plugins/provider-validation.ts` — deprecated discovery provider warnings
- `src/channels/streaming-flat-key-deprecation.ts` — flat streaming key deprecation
- `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-config.ts` — deprecated config API warnings
- `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts` — rejected config domain warnings
- `pnpm test src/plugins/provider-validation.test.ts src/channels/streaming-flat-key-deprecation.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-config.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts` — 43 passed, 0 regressions
- `pnpm test src/infra/dedupe.test.ts` — createDedupeCache eviction behavior: after maxSize entries, check() evicts oldest half and returns false for new keys, keeping memory bounded

target.title: fix(tasks): add bounded queryTaskRecords to avoid O(N) clone in tasks.list (fixes #105425)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`listTaskRecordsUnsorted` clones every retained task record — O(N) heap allocation. The gateway `tasks.list` handler then filters, sorts, and paginates the clone to ≤500 rows. On installations with thousands of retained tasks, this causes unbounded memory pressure for every tasks.list API call.

Fixes #105425.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `queryTaskRecords` — a new bounded query that applies filter, sort, and pagination inside the registry before cloning. Only the returned page is deep-cloned. A `findFirstTaskRecord` helper is also added for callers that only need the first match.

The gateway `tasks.list` handler now uses `queryTaskRecords` instead of `listTaskRecordsUnsorted().filter().toSorted().slice()`.

## User Impact

Operators with large task registries see reduced GC pressure during task-list API calls. The API response is unchanged — same filter, same sort, same pagination.

## Evidence

- `src/tasks/task-registry.ts` — `queryTaskRecords` + `findFirstTaskRecord`
- `src/tasks/runtime-internal.ts` — both exported
- `src/gateway/server-methods/tasks.ts` — gateway caller updated to use `queryTaskRecords`
- `pnpm test src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/tasks.test.ts` — 139 passed, 0 regressions

target.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws status [claw-or-agent]` with canonical agent, workspace-file, package, session, and scheduled-job state
- bind `claws remove` consent to a dry-run `planIntegrity` digest and revalidate the complete removal surface before mutation
- recover and expose orphaned subordinate provenance even when the root install row or agent config is missing
- serialize package lifecycle mutations across processes; skill mutations are serialized per workspace because they share one ClawHub lockfile
- treat plugins as global: Claw removal releases plugin references but does not uninstall the plugin; workspace-scoped skills remain eligible for safe final-reference removal

## Scope

This is the status/remove slice for the grouped one-Claw/one-agent contract. Package names resolve an install only when unambiguous; final agent ids always work and disambiguate repeated adds.

Remove is plan-first. Dry-run binds agent identity and config-removal surfaces, route bindings, agent-to-agent allow entries, scheduled-job blockers, managed-file digests, package ownership, workspace/agent/session cleanup targets, and root install state into `planIntegrity`. Apply requires `--yes --plan-integrity <digest>`, rebuilds the plan, and fails closed if consent-bearing input changed.

Missing managed files are treated as already removed; locally modified or untracked operator files are retained. Canonical workspace, agent-state, and session paths are validated and staged before deletion. Partial cleanup retains subordinate provenance for status/retry rather than inventing a permanent removal tombstone.

Plugins are global OpenClaw resources. Removing a Claw emits an explicit retain reason and releases only that Claw's plugin reference. Skills are workspace-scoped: a final unchanged Claw-installed skill can be removed through the canonical ClawHub skill lifecycle, while shared, adopted, drifted, incomplete, provenance-ambiguous, or otherwise uncertain skills are retained.

All commands remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, and JSON contracts remain experimental.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102228 package installation, ownership, and references
- This PR: lifecycle visibility and consent-bound cleanup
- Next: #102306 portable export from the same provenance ledger

## Validation

Exact head: `da8e4d41d73c77c6294e8813ac2856ad402a646b`

- 49 focused lifecycle/package/ownership/skill-uninstall unit tests passed
- targeted canonical ClawHub plugin-install lease test passed
- real `add -> status -> remove dry-run -> digest-bound remove` CLI E2E passed with the dedicated E2E config
- scoped TypeScript check: no PR-local errors
- Oxlint clean across all changed TypeScript files
- Oxfmt and `git diff --check` clean
- `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox review --uncommitted`: no discrete actionable regressions

## Real behavior proof

`src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts` invokes the real `src/entry.ts` CLI in an isolated state directory and passes the complete add, status, removal preview, and digest-bound removal flow. The final result is `openclaw.clawRemoveResult.v1` with `status: "complete"`; canonical agent config is removed and the unchanged managed workspace file is deleted.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenCode Zen users could not discover or resolve the `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-sol` models even though OpenCode's live model catalog already advertised them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider-owned Zen catalog now includes the three live GPT-5.6 routes with their OpenCode routing, context/output limits, pricing tiers, and supported reasoning efforts. The OpenCode thinking policy also exposes those declared `xhigh` and `max` levels while leaving proxied Claude profiles unchanged.

## User Impact

OpenCode Zen users can now see and select all three GPT-5.6 tiers through OpenClaw model discovery, including when the static catalog fallback is used, without `xhigh` or `max` being silently clamped to `high`.

## Evidence

- Third-party live red: `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` returned `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-sol`; the OpenClaw live catalog contract failed with those exact three IDs reported as missing static metadata.
- Credentialed third-party live suite: both OpenCode live tests passed, covering catalog alignment plus a real tool-call/reasoning replay through the provider.
- Credentialed OpenClaw CLI E2E: `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-sol` were each invoked with `--thinking max` through `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/responses`; all calls returned HTTP 200 with reasoning-token usage and `aborted: false`.
- OpenClaw CLI E2E on the final commit: the repository source completed its TypeScript and bundled-plugin build, then `models list --provider opencode --json` returned 55 models including all three GPT-5.6 routes with 1,050,000-token context windows. The command used isolated OpenClaw state directories.
- Review reproduction red: both the bundled public policy artifact and registered provider surface silently omitted `xhigh`/`max` for the new GPT-5.6 routes; focused tests failed 2 cases.
- Review fix green: the same focused policy tests passed 18/18, including `max` remaining available with the provider-owned profile.
- OpenCode extension suite: 5 files, 35/35 tests passed.
- Extension source and extension-test typechecks passed.
- Targeted oxlint, oxfmt check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- After ClawSweeper review, the focused public-policy test was simplified to use only the fields needed by the assertion; its focused test and the extension test-type lane passed again.
- The aggregate `check:changed` wrapper could not reach its checks because its delegated Testbox dependency install hit the host's file-descriptor limit while fetching unrelated optional platform packages; the corresponding scoped typecheck/lint/test lanes above were run directly. Full hosted gates remain owned by PR CI.

All CLI and live verification used the OpenClaw repository source; it did not invoke Co-Claw.

target.title: fix(telegram-miniapp): cancel unread response body on auth error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Telegram Mini App page receives a non-ok HTTP response (e.g., 401 auth error), the response body stream is left dangling without being cancelled. This can leak connections and waste resources in the Mini App's WebView environment.

**Root Cause**: The `renderTelegramMiniAppPage()` function's `fetch("auth", ...)` handler was missing `response.body?.cancel()` before `throw new Error("auth failed")`, leaving the response body stream unread and un-cancelled on auth errors.

**Solution**: Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw, matching the established codebase pattern used across `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts`, `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, and other extensions.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Local HTTP server simulating Telegram auth endpoint (401 response), Node.js `fetch` API.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# L2 simulation: auth endpoint returning 401, verify cancel() is called
node docs/.local/issue-109983/verify.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence** (`docs/.local/issue-109983/verify.log`):
```
PASS: response.body.cancel() called on auth error, no unhandled rejection
PASS: response.status = 401 (expected 401)
PASS: response.ok = false (expected false)
PASS: body stream is closed after cancel (done=true)
PASS: repeated cancel() is idempotent
ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 5 checks pass, confirming:
1. `cancel()` is called without unhandled rejection on auth error (401)
2. After `cancel()`, the body stream reports `done=true` (stream properly closed)
3. Repeated `cancel()` calls are idempotent and do not throw

**What was not tested**: Real Telegram WebView environment — the `cancel()` call is browser/WebView API (`ReadableStream.cancel()`), which is simulated here via Node.js `fetch` (which implements the same Web API). ## Summary

**What changed**: Added `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw in `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` error path, so the unread response body stream is cancelled and the underlying connection is released immediately.

**What NOT changed**: No change to any other provider (OpenAI, Bedrock, etc.). No change to success paths. No change to retry or timeout logic. No new dependencies.

Fixes #109978

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` receives a non-OK HTTP response (e.g. 403, 429, 500), the `response.body` readable stream remains unconsumed. Node.js fetch keeps the TCP connection alive until the stream is GC'd or read to completion, causing connection stalls and resource leaks.

**Root Cause**: Missing `response.body.cancel()` in the error path of `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` in `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.ts`.

**Solution**: Call `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing the error. The optional chaining handles null-body responses gracefully. The `.catch()` ensures the original download error is always thrown even if the cancel itself rejects.

target.title: fix(cron): stop a cron job's own marker from blocking its awaited wake
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A `wakeMode: "now"` main-session cron job can block the heartbeat it owns. The job installs its active execution marker before awaiting `runHeartbeatOnce`; the heartbeat admission guard then sees cron work in progress and rejects the owning wake. A manual `cron.run` adds a second self-block because its queued `CommandLane.Cron` task also counts as unrelated lane pressure. Cron falls back to an asynchronous request and records success before delivery is confirmed.

This is a deterministic defect found while investigating #105257. It fixes the reproducible self-block; it does not claim to close that broader intermittent report.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron path now carries two exact, private ownership markers into the heartbeat runner:

- the active cron execution marker `{ jobId, token }`;
- the current Cron command-lane task marker `{ lane, taskId, generation }` for queued Gateway `cron.run` calls.

Heartbeat admission discounts only markers that still match the authoritative active job and lane task. Another cron job, another queued Cron task, any `CronNested` task, a same-ID replacement, or a stale marker still blocks the wake. Scheduled and direct owners receive no lane exemption. The public plugin heartbeat facade cannot supply or forge either internal marker.

Exact identity matters. Broadly discounting a lane count or job ID would let unrelated or superseded work bypass the existing admission fence.

## User Impact

Main-session `wakeMode: "now"` cron runs now wait for their owned heartbeat delivery before recording terminal success. Other cron work continues to enforce the existing concurrency fence. No config, storage, protocol, or public plugin API changes.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage exercises the full decision surface:

- exact active marker, unrelated marker, same-ID replacement, and stale replacement;
- exact Cron-lane task, a second Cron task, `CronNested`, and stale lane generations;
- direct manual run, Gateway-queued `cron.run`, and natural scheduled firing;
- real heartbeat runner integration and Gateway adapter forwarding;
- marker and command-lane cleanup before sandbox deletion.

Results:

- 100 focused tests passed across the Gateway adapter, heartbeat runner, cron wake integration, and command queue.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed on Blacksmith Testbox ([run 29632824782](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29632824782)).
- Exact-head hosted CI is green.
- Fresh autoreview found no actionable issue.

Live proof used the official OpenAI API with `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, an isolated QA state root, and a custom loopback Gateway port (`41103`):

- Natural timer: outbound delivery `1784347997662`, terminal success `1784347997665`.
- Real Gateway `cron.run`: outbound delivery `1784348000474`, terminal success `1784348000476`.
- Both successful one-shots were deleted.

The timestamp ordering is the regression oracle: the old self-block records terminal success before the later asynchronous outbound message; the fixed path delivers first.

## Scope

`next-heartbeat` remains asynchronous by design. Issue #105257 remains open for its broader intermittent payload-loss report.

---

🤖 AI-assisted: original fix by @harjothkhara, reviewed and rewritten with maintainer tests, changed-gate proof, and live OpenAI Gateway verification.
